issuing_authority: New Mexico Board of Licensure for Professional Engineers and Professional Surveyors
source_title: Minimum Standards for Surveying in New Mexico
revision_date: Relevant provisions amended 2016-07-24; current text reviewed 2026-08-02
uas_topic: Professional surveying; photogrammetry; digital geospatial data; accuracy; reporting
regulated_party: New Mexico professional surveyors and professional engineers authorized to perform surveying
regulated_activity: Using UAV/UAS sensor data in work that constitutes professional surveying
requirement_type: Professional-practice classification, competency, accuracy, reporting, certification, and recordation standards
permit_or_approval_required: No UAS-specific permit; applicable surveying work must be performed within authorized professional practice and satisfy the rule
commercial_operator_relevance: High for surveying deliverables; moderate for data collection supplied to a licensed professional
summary: New Mexico's minimum surveying standards expressly include digital geospatial data produced by UAV/UAS and airborne sensors. When a licensed surveyor—or an engineer authorized by the Engineering and Surveying Practice Act—undertakes surveying, the licensee must classify the work and follow the corresponding standards. Topographic maps must meet current ASPRS positional-accuracy standards and carry prescribed accuracy reporting; control surveys relied on by other professionals require a report with coordinates, datum, methods, dates, accuracy, and certification. Boundary, easement, and right-of-way work carries additional field, plat, supervision, certification, and sometimes recordation requirements. The rule does not make every drone-derived image a professional survey.
verification_status: Verified against current official NMAC text
notes: Mission scope and intended deliverable determine whether collected UAS data enters regulated surveying practice. The rule identifies UAV/UAS data as a data source but regulates the professional surveying service and work product, not flight by itself.

geographic_scope: Statewide where protected species may be affected or information may support hunting
source_title: Use of aircraft and drones in hunting and wildlife management
uas_topic: Wildlife harassment; hunting assistance; wildlife-location information; management exemption
regulated_party: Any person using an aircraft or drone around protected species or supplying location information for hunting
regulated_activity: Harassing protected species, locating them by drone, relaying their location, or using drone-derived location information to aid a take
requirement_type: Prohibition with a director-issued management exemption
permit_or_approval_required: No approval for unrelated work; the Director may exempt a person for management purposes
aec_relevance: Moderate to high for environmental, ecological, and remote-area missions
summary: New Mexico prohibits pursuing, harassing, driving, or rallying protected species except as lawful hunting or otherwise authorized by wildlife law. It also prohibits using an aircraft or drone to spot or locate protected species and relay the location to anyone on the ground. No person may hunt, take, or assist in hunting or taking a protected species with location information gained from a drone at any time; the comparable aircraft restriction lasts 48 hours. The Department Director may grant an exemption for management purposes. Ordinary engineering, inspection, mapping, or environmental collection is not automatically hunting assistance, but flight conduct and later disclosure or reuse of wildlife-location data can trigger the rule.
verification_status: Verified against current official NMAC text
notes: The rule defines drone broadly. A project involving intentional wildlife management should resolve the Director-exemption pathway before fieldwork.

summary: New Mexico's park rule authorizes each superintendent to restrict or prohibit activities in specified park areas by posting or other designation; it does not itself state a blanket statewide drone ban. The Division's live alerts use that authority for drone-specific prohibitions. As reviewed, Bottomless Lakes and Rio Grande Nature Center have ongoing notices citing 19.5.2.9(C), and other individual park pages identify drone use as prohibited. Because the restriction list is dynamic and park-specific, a team should check the current alert and the exact park's page before mobilization and obtain written direction when commercial access, takeoff, landing, or an exception is proposed.
verification_status: Verified against current official NMAC text and live State Parks restriction page
notes: Examples are evidence of how 19.5.2.9(C) is implemented, not an exhaustive permanent list. Navajo Lake and several individual park pages also identify drone use as prohibited.

geographic_scope: NMSU premises systemwide and NMSU-resource UAS operations on or off university premises
uas_topic: University approval; third-party operations; insurance; procurement; privacy; incident reporting
regulated_party: NMSU units and non-university persons or organizations operating on or over NMSU premises
regulated_activity: Operating, purchasing, registering, insuring, or reporting incidents involving UAS within the policy's scope
requirement_type: Prior written authorization, documentation, sponsorship, registration, insurance, training, and procurement review
permit_or_approval_required: Yes — final written EHS&RM authorization; third parties also require an NMSU sponsoring department
public_agency_only: No — expressly covers third parties on or over university premises
summary: NMSU prohibits launching, landing, or flying a UAS within University Premises without University approval and applies the policy to outside parties. Outdoor requests use the Flight Request Form, normally submitted 3–10 business days before the activity, and authorization is not complete until EHS&RM gives final written approval. A third party needs an NMSU sponsoring department and supporting operator, aircraft, insurance, and safety documentation. The policy also restricts recording in private or sensitive spaces, requires incident reporting, and subjects grant or contract terms involving UAS purchase or flight to EHS&RM review for federally banned systems and systems not authorized in other states. University-resource aircraft have additional registration, insurance, training, and disposition requirements.
verification_status: Verified against current official NMSU policy and linked flight-operations guidance
notes: Third-party flight-operations guidance calls for supporting items including insurance, FAA registration, Part 107 credentials, and a safety plan. Project teams should retrieve the current form and tier requirements for each request.

issuing_authority: University of New Mexico Risk Services
citation: UNM Risk Services drone-flight approval requirements
uas_topic: University property; prior approval; pilot credentials; insurance; flight planning
regulated_party: Any operator flying over University-owned property and users of University-owned aircraft
regulated_activity: Conducting a drone operation over University property or using a University-owned drone
permit_or_approval_required: Yes — prior University approval through the Risk Services request form
aec_relevance: High for campus, facility, roofing, construction, and infrastructure assignments
summary: The University of New Mexico requires prior approval for every drone operation over University-owned property and every operation involving a University-owned aircraft. Its Risk Services request asks for pilot information including a Part 107 certificate, any certificate of authorization, aviation or drone liability-insurance evidence, acknowledgement of FAA commercial-operation requirements, and a complete flight plan. The University directs applicants to submit the form at least two weeks before the planned flight. University-owned drones must be insured through Risk Services before flight. An outside commercial team should treat the approval and lead time as mission prerequisites and confirm the property boundary and current documentary requirements before scheduling fieldwork.
verification_status: Verified against current official UNM Risk Services page
notes: The page is an approval requirement rather than a statute. The live request form may collect additional fields, so retrieve it for the planned operation.
